title: A Veil for the Oath
premise: Theo Winterbourne fled her hedge-witch master with a stolen grimoire and a talent for numbers, finding uneasy refuge as ledger-keeper for the Gilded Veil, a guild that brokers impossible things: bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When prayers start being answered by gods everyone believed dead, the guild's clients turn desperate and dangerous, and Theo discovers the ledgers record more than trades — they are a binding contract that has kept the old gods sleeping. To protect the ragtag found family she never meant to make, Theo must conceal that her own bloodline is the final seal on the divine prison, a secret that could reignite the god-war while the last dragon's fire — the only force able to reforge the broken oath — gutters toward extinction. In the end, Theo chooses to burn the ledgers and offer herself as the new living veil, but her guildmates refuse to let her stand alone, sharing the burden of the oath among them and proving that duty shared is no longer duty that corrupts.
about_author: Beatrix Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about people who keep dangerous books, and lives quietly with two cats named after minor deities.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We meet the Gilded Veil through its accounts: a widow buying one hour of her drowned husband's voice, a mercenary trading his shadow. Theo balances the books and keeps her head down, haunted by the grimoire she stole from her former master. Emotional beat: wary belonging — she has found shelter but trusts nothing.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in Ash
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A client prays at a wayside shrine and something answers — the first miracle in three hundred years. The guild's mistress, Vespera Quill, orders the client silenced; Theo secretly copies the incident into a private ledger. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a traitorous thrill of wonder.

chapters.title: What the Grimoire Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with an interlude from her old master Aldous. Studying her stolen grimoire, Theo realizes its spells are accounting entries — debits against a divine prison. Aldous, tracking her, learns the same and begins selling the knowledge. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Guild of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through guild members: Bramble the forger, Sister Ondine the ex-priestess, Kesh the dragon-blooded courier. A raid by Aldous's agents forces them to flee together, and Theo sees them, for the first time, as family rather than colleagues. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under fire.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Guttering
chapters.summary: Kesh's POV. The group seeks the last dragon, Ember-that-Was, whose fire alone can reforge the broken oath. They find her ancient, half-blind, and dying — and she recognizes something in Theo's blood that makes her weep smoke. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by mortality.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margins
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Deciphering marginalia in the oldest ledger, Theo learns the truth: her bloodline wrote the original binding, and every entry she has balanced has been feeding the seal. She hides it from the others. Emotional beat: isolation — love against the growing weight of duty.

chapters.title: Aldous Ascendant
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Having sold god-secrets to a warlord cult, Aldous offers Theo absolution and partnership: rule beside him as the gods' new stewards. His power is seductive precisely because he frames corruption as stewardship. Emotional beat: temptation — the theme of power's corruption made personal.

chapters.title: The Unbalancing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The cult breaches the Veil's vaults; Vespera falls protecting the ledgers, and Theo's secret spills out in the chaos — Bramble and Ondine learn what she hid. Betrayal and fury, then Ondine's quiet forgiveness. Emotional beat: rupture and the first mending.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Theo and Kesh POVs. At the shattered shrine-mountain, Aldous opens the prison; the first god stirs. Theo writes herself into the ledger as the new living seal while Ember spends her final fire to reforge the oath. The others seize the pen with her, splitting the burden. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into shared covenant.

chapters.title: A Veil Worn Together
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. The gods sleep again, held not by one bloodline but by five keepers who balance the books together. The guild rebuilds around a hearth instead of a vault; Theo finally reads her own name without flinching. Emotional beat: resolution — duty shared, love chosen, power kept honest.
